task: After a non-silent codemie self-update, verify the first codemie on PATH runs the just-installed version and print a clear warning if not (EPMCDME-16080).

key_reasoning.reason: Closest patterns are native-installer verifyInstallation (version probe via exec), hook-command resolveBinary (Windows .cmd shim swap) and getCommandPath (first PATH match). None covers the hard constraint: the spawned `codemie --version` re-enters bin/codemie.js and runs the start-up update flow, so a stale binary could self-install into its own prefix or prompt. The only existing skip switches are test-env flags (NODE_ENV=test / VITEST), --json argv and hook argv, and CODEMIE_AUTO_UPDATE=false prompts rather than skipping. Windows adds the extensionless shim, shell:true quoting of paths with spaces, and a timeout that may not kill the grandchild. Acceptance details (cross-platform, silent vs non-silent, exit code stays 0) are enumerated, and no existing test covers the non-silent success path or the PATH logic.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk set to L: no exact precedent for suppressing the child's auto-update, plus child-process side effects (self-update by a stale binary, prompt, update lock).
